reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes Forsage participation through a personal referral link and ID while presenting earnings as proof of the opportunity. The profile screens pair BUSD profit figures with partner, team, ratio, and priority-leader indicators, encouraging viewers to join a recruitment-based structure rather than merely discussing it.

opening.argument: Judge the claim at the level actually shown. “Earning Proof” presents a purported past result, not a promise that a viewer will earn the same amount. The dashboard displays a profit figure, but a displayed figure is not verification of a payout or a guarantee of future returns. The supplied speech adds only a closing thanks. The link may invite interest, yet these sources do not show the creator assuring viewers that joining is risk-free or that earnings are certain. Treat the figures as an unverified personal claim, not as evidence of a guaranteed-income pitch.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution rightly identifies a personal link and ID, but their presence does not establish what a viewer is promised for using them. Nor do the dashboard’s profit and network indicators establish that the displayed profit was paid out, or that it depends on recruiting others. Those are important gaps when deciding whether this is a deceptive earnings solicitation rather than a presentation of account information.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: An explicit guarantee is not necessary to recognize this promotion. The title pairs “Earning Proof” with the creator’s ID and participation link; the account screen then places a profit figure beside partner and team counts, a shareable personal link, and “Join Priority Leaders.” The defense is right that a screenshot cannot verify a payout, but lack of verification does not make the earnings-and-recruitment presentation neutral.

opening.argument: This can be read as an account demonstration rather than an instruction to join. The sampled screen shows an interface with a profile, a personal link, a profit panel, and partner and team counters—features a viewer might inspect to understand what the account displays. The description even opens a question about the program. The supplied transcript contains no spoken enrollment instructions, only a sign-off. A demonstration may show promotional features without itself explaining, endorsing, or proving an income mechanism.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution reads the counters as encouragement to enter a recruitment structure. But showing where an interface puts its partner and team counts is also consistent with demonstrating the account. “Join Priority Leaders” appears on that interface; the supplied speech does not show the creator explaining it as a route to earnings. The title’s “Earning Proof” is a strong promotional cue, but it does not by itself resolve what the demonstration establishes.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The demonstration reading leaves out the video’s framing. The title does not merely name an interface: it calls the display “Earning Proof” and supplies the creator’s ID and referral URL. The sampled account screen repeats the personal link alongside profits, partner and team counts, and “Join Priority Leaders.” A viewer is given both an earnings claim and a path to participate, not just an explanation of how a screen works.

opening.argument: A personal referral link is not, on its own, proof of a scam mechanism. Here the title supplies an ID and URL, while the account screen shows a shareable link, profit figures, and network counts. None of those sampled details specifies a required deposit, states a guaranteed return, requests a viewer’s credentials, or explains that income is paid for recruiting a downline. The material may promote a service, but the visible evidence does not establish the transaction terms or the source of the displayed profits. The judge should not fill those gaps with an assumed mechanism.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution connects the displayed BUSD profit to partners, team, ratio, and a join prompt. Proximity on one account screen, however, does not show how profits are calculated or whether recruiting causes them. The title’s referral URL establishes a route to the site, not the terms a visitor would encounter there. Those missing steps matter before treating the counters as proof of recruitment commissions.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The prosecution need not prove the complete payment formula to assess what this video promotes. It presents “Earning Proof” next to a personal referral URL, and the account view combines purported profits with partner and team counts, a personal link with sharing controls, and “Join Priority Leaders.” The defense identifies details the video does not establish, but those gaps do not erase its invitation to approach an earnings opportunity through a network-linked account.
